[By Public Prosecutor]
 ORDER

The petitioner has filed the petition U/s 438 of the Cr.PC seeking for grant of anticipatory bail in respect of the offence alleged against him U/s 420 of IPC registered in Crl.Misc.No.25286/2023 Cr.No.23/2023 dated 11.02.2023 by the respondent Byyappanhalli Police station.

2. Brief facts of the case of the petitioner is that the complainant Sri. N. Mohan in his complaint has alleged that he was introduced to the Accused No.1 through the petitioner stating that the accused No.1 was searching to purchase sites at Devanahalli.

The complainant showed site formed at Sri.Rama Enclave Layout and the accused No.1 informed the complainant that she is employed as Captain, Military Engineering Services, DRDO Complex, CV Raman Nagar, Bengaluru and required a developer for constructing buildings at Vishwa, Akash Vihar, Marathahalli and Alisda.
The accused No.1 has also told the complainant that she would call tender for works worth of Rs.66 crores and asked him to apply for the same.
The accused No.2 Crl.Misc.No.25286/2023 lured the complainant to get the tender work she had financial transaction with the accused No.1.

It is further alleged in the complaint that on 21.10.2022 the accused No.1 called the complainant to the Estate Management Unit situated at DRDO complex, C.V. Raman Nagar and informed him that the Military Engineering Services (G.E) has called for a tender and informed him to upload his Sri.P.R.Darshan vs No.2:- S/O B.R.Rajanna on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45016874/
1 documents pertaining to Eden Gold Properties and Constructions and after completing the formalities, she informed him that the contract has been awarded to him and asked him to pay 2%
security deposit in two installments on or before 08.11.2022.

Accordingly, the complainant paid an amount of Rs.72,000/- and Rs.10 lakhs by way of cash and he also transferred a sum of Rs.35 lakhs,
Rs.5 lakhs and Rs.16 lakhs through RTGS to the account of accused No.1.
Later the Crl.Misc.No.25286/2023 accused No.1 also lured the complainant to pay Rs.20 lakhs by way of cash, hence the complainant had totally paid Rs.1,16,72,500/- to the accused No.1.
Later the complainant on enquiry came to know that the accused No.1 is not employee of the DRDO and he was conned by the accused No.1 and 2.
Hence, the complainant has filed the complaint before the Byappanahalli police.
3. The prosecution has filed objections to this application.
In the objections the prosecution has stated that the complaint and the materials on record prima-facie show that the commission of the offences by the petitioner/accused.
The investigation is under progress and the petitioner is still absconding.
If the petitioner is released on bail, there are chances of the petitioner further absconding and delaying the trial.
The petitioner may repeat the similar offences and threaten the Crl.Misc.No.25286/2023 Prosecution witnesses.
Therefore, the Prosecution has prayed to reject the bail application.

4. Heard and perused the case papers.
5.

Now, the point that arises for my consideration is:-
1. Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of anticipatory bail as sought for?
2. What order?

6. My answer to the above points are as under:-
Point No.1 : In the affirmative Point No.2 :

As per the final order for the following:-
REASONS 7.Point No.1:-

The respondent police has filed the case against accused No.1 and 2 based on the complaint lodged by Sri. N. Mohan alleging that the accused No.1 was acquainted with the accused No.2 and the accused No.2 Crl.Misc.No.25286/2023 had introduced the complainant to the accused No.1 for purchasing site at Devanahalli and during the course of the said transaction the accused No.1 enticed the complainant to apply for tender work for construction of buildings and residential area.
The accused No.1 had obtained documents from the complainant in respect of the tender bearing I.D:2022-GE-469253-9 and issued a security deposit receipt which is signed by the accused No.1.
The accused No.1 also informed the complainant to pay 2% of the security deposit in two instalments, failing which, she informed the complainant that the tender would be cancelled.

The complainant paid an amount of Rs.72,000/- and Rs.10 lakhs by way of cash and sum of Rs.35 lakhs,
Rs.5 lakhs and Rs.16 lakhs through RTGS to the account of accused No.1.
Later on 23.11.2022 the Sri.P.R.Darshan vs No.2:-

S/O B.R.Rajanna on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45016874/
2 complainant again paid Rs.30 lakhs to the accused No.1.
In total, the Crl.Misc.No.25286/2023 complainant has paid 1,16,72,500/- to the accused No.1.
Later when the complainant enquired the DRDO office about the tender work, he came to know that the person by name of accused No.1 was not employed at DRDO office.

8. The learned counsel for the petitioner has argued that the complainant has paid the alleged amount upon demand made by the accused No.1 and there is no element of cheating to constitute the offence U/s 420 of IPC against the accused No.2.

Further it is also argued by the counsel that the accused No.1 has also deceived the accused No.2/petitioner and has extracted Rs.45 lakhs from the petitioner and his father by executing loan agreements in favor of Sri. Jyotirmoy Daimari, the husband of the accused No.1 who is the director of Lotahill Services Crl.Misc.No.25286/2023 Private Limited and as such the accused No.2/petitioner is also a victim at the hands of the accused No.1.

9. On considering the entire records it can be seen that except for the allegation made against the accused No.2/petitioner that he had introduced the accused No.1 to the complainant and lured the complainant to get tender work, no other allegation has been made against the accused No.2.

It is not the case of the complainant that he has paid Rs.1,16,72,500/- to the accused No.2.
10.

The learned counsel for the petitioner hs relied upoon the decision reported in (2023) 1 SCC 178 (Sunita Devi and another Vs. State of Haryana) and has also produced the notice issued to the petitioner under sec.41(A) of the Cr.P.C and argued that after the issuance of the notice dtd.
2.3.2023, the petitoner had assisted in the investigation also.

entities.text: (2023) 1 SCC 178 (Sunita Devi and another Vs. State of Haryana)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The issuance of the notice u/s.41(A) of the Criminal Procedure Code goes to show that the chances of the petitioner/accused No.2 being arrested cannot be ruled out.

The petitioner had produced the copies of the loan agreement entered by the petitioner and his father with Lotohill Services Pvt. Ltd.
12.

Hence, considering the materials on record, admittedly, the offence alleged against the petitioner is not punishable with imprisonment for life or death and triable by the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class.

Also considering that the transaction is in the nature of money transaction, which are to be decided mainly on the documentary evidence in the full fledged trial, hence, considering the above materials on record, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds Crl.Misc.No.25286/2023 for grant an order of anticipatory bail in his favour.
Accordingly, the point No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
13. Point No.2:-

In view of the reasonings given above, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER

The bail petition filed by the petitioner/ accused No.2 under Sec.438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is hereby allowed by granting an order of anticipatory bail, subject to the following conditions:-
Sri.
P.R.Darshan

vs No.2:- S/O B.R.Rajanna on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45016874/
3 1) The petitioner shall give attendance before the I.O on every first Sunday of the month between 10 a.m. and 2 p.m., for a period of three months or till the Final Report/Charge sheet is filed, whichever is earlier.

Crl.Misc.No.25286/2023 2) The petitioner shall appear before the trial Court and file regular bail application within one month from the date of this order.
3) The petitioner shall not commit similar offences or other offences.
4) The petitioner shall appear before the trial Court on all hearing dates without fail.
5) The petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Court without prior permission.
6) The petitioner shall not threaten the prosecution witnesses or tamper with the prosecution evidence and shall co-operate in the investigation.

Crl.Misc.No.25286/2023 7) The petitioner shall furnish proof of his residential address and shall inform the court if there is any change in the address.
8) The petitioner, in the event of his arrest in Crime No.23/2023 of Byappanahalli Police station, he shall be released on bail on obtaining his personal bond for Rs.1,00,000/- with one surety for the like sum, who is not a senior citizen.
Violation of any of the conditions, the bail bond stands forfeited automatically.
